metadata.description: AzBrief Enterprise — Microsoft Foundry Hosted Agent analysis runtime + Container Apps control plane and scheduler + Communication Services, with Key Vault backed secrets and Entra-only Foundry auth.
Base name used to derive every resource name. 3-16 lowercase alphanumeric characters.
Location for the regional resources. Defaults to the resource group location.
Tags applied to every resource.
Region for the Microsoft Foundry account. Model availability differs by region — keep the default unless the chosen model is unavailable there.
Model deployment name used by the agents.
Model to deploy into the Foundry account.
Model version. Leave empty to let Azure pick the default version for the model.
Model deployment SKU.

Model deployment capacity in thousands of tokens per minute (TPM). A single report prompt alone runs ~27K tokens, and the multi-agent stages, planning and execution share the same deployment, so 30 rate-limits every run.
Name of the Foundry Hosted Agent that owns the complete analysis and subscriber-customization runtime. Deploy this name from azure.yaml before starting the Container App or scheduler.
Container image for the orchestrator/Admin Page. The default is a placeholder — deploy the real AzBrief image afterwards (see the deployContainerImageCommand output).
Optional private registry login server (e.g. myacr.azurecr.io) pulled with the managed identity. Leave empty for public images.
Minimum replica count. 1 keeps the orchestrator warm; 0 scales to zero between runs.
Maximum replica count.
Optional CIDR allow-list for the Container App ingress. Empty means any source may reach the ingress (authentication still applies).
Existing subnet resource ID for Container Apps infrastructure (VNet integration). Overrides the subnet the template would otherwise use. Leave empty to let Azure manage the network.
Make the Container App ingress internal (VNet-only). The scheduled job calls Foundry directly, while /admin, /api/*, and /mcp then resolve only from inside the virtual network.

How the topology is protected on the network. "vnetInjection" (default) injects the Foundry agents and the Container App into a virtual network and reaches Foundry, Key Vault and the state account over private endpoints. "perimeter" keeps public endpoints but wraps Foundry, Key Vault and Log Analytics in a Network Security Perimeter. "public" keeps public endpoints with authentication as the only boundary — evaluation use only. Foundry network injection cannot be added after the account exists, so switching to vnetInjection later requires deleting and purging the account.

Keep the Foundry data plane reachable from the public internet even in vnetInjection mode. An agent can only be created from a network that can reach the data plane, so the roster cannot be provisioned from a workstation once the account is closed. Turn this on for the initial setup, then redeploy with it off. Agent network injection and the private endpoints are unaffected either way.

Existing virtual network resource ID used when networkIsolationMode is vnetInjection. Leave empty to have the template create one. When supplied, the three subnets named below must already exist with the delegations described in their descriptions.
Address space of the virtual network the template creates. Must sit inside an RFC1918 range — the Foundry agent subnet rejects anything else.
Subnet dedicated to Foundry agent network injection. Delegated to Microsoft.App/environments and never shared with a second Foundry account.
Address prefix for the Foundry agent subnet. /24 is the size Microsoft recommends for this delegation.
Subnet hosting the Container Apps environment. Delegated to Microsoft.App/environments.
Address prefix for the Container Apps subnet. /27 is the documented minimum for a workload profiles environment.
Subnet holding the Foundry and Key Vault private endpoints. Must not be delegated.
Address prefix for the private endpoint subnet.
Access mode of the Network Security Perimeter associations. Learning (Transition) logs without blocking — read NSPAccessLogs first, then redeploy with Enforced.
Inbound CIDR ranges allowed through the Network Security Perimeter. Empty means no IP-based exception.
Subscription IDs whose managed identities may reach the perimeter resources. Empty defaults to the deployment subscription, which is what lets the Container App call Foundry.
Outbound FQDNs the perimeter resources may call. Defaults to the two domains AzBrief itself allows for document fetching.
Entra ID application (client) ID for Admin Page sign-in. Leave empty to keep the Admin Page disabled.
Client secret for the Admin Page app registration. Required when adminEntraClientId is set.
Comma-separated allow-list of admin principals (UPN/email or object ID). Required for the Admin Page to serve anything.
Comma-separated allow-list of Archive Page readers (UPN/email, object ID, or group ID). Administrators are readers automatically.
Data residency for Communication Services.
Fallback recipient address used when no subscriber list is configured.
Subscriber list as a JSON array, e.g. [{"email":"a@co.com","name":"A","role":"Cloud Architect","language":"ko"}].
Cron expression, in UTC, for the daily digest job. Default: 02:00 UTC every day.
Seconds a single job execution may run before Container Apps stops it. Keep RUN_TIME_BUDGET_S below this so the run defers leftover updates and commits its checkpoint before the replica is killed.
API key protecting the orchestrator endpoint. A random value is generated when left at the default.
Enable Key Vault purge protection. Recommended for production; note that a purge-protected vault cannot be deleted for the retention period.
Key Vault soft-delete retention in days.
Log Analytics retention in days.

properties.contentType: Entra ID app registration client secret (Admin Page)

properties.description: Hosted Agent runtime and Prompt Agent roster for Azure Update analysis

configuration.secrets: [concat(createArray(createObject('name', 'acs-connection-string', 'keyVaultUrl', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets', variables('keyVaultName'), 'acs-connection-string'), '2023-07-01').secretUri, 'identity', resourceId('Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities', variables('managedIdentityName'))), createObject('name', 'orchestrator-api-key', 'keyVaultUrl', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets', variables('keyVaultName'), 'orchestrator-api-key'), '2023-07-01').secretUri, 'identity', resourceId('Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities', variables('managedIdentityName')))), if(variables('adminAuthConfigured'), createArray(createObject('name', 'microsoft-provider-authentication-secret', 'keyVaultUrl', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets', variables('keyVaultName'), 'admin-entra-client-secret'), '2023-07-01').secretUri, 'identity', resourceId('Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities', variables('managedIdentityName')))), createArray()))]

metadata.description: Wildcard private DNS zone that resolves an internal Container Apps environment inside the virtual network.
Container Apps environment default domain. Becomes the private DNS zone name.
Static IP of the environment load balancer that the wildcard record points at.
Virtual network the zone is linked to.
Suffix used to name the virtual network link.
Tags applied to the zone.
Private DNS zone that resolves the internal environment.
Container App URL hosting the orchestrator API, Admin Page, and MCP surface.

containerAppUrl.value: [if(variables('internalIngress'), format('{0} (VNet-only — reachable from inside the virtual network)', format('https://{0}', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.App/containerApps', variables('containerAppName')), '2024-03-01').configuration.ingress.fqdn)), format('https://{0}', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.App/containerApps', variables('containerAppName')), '2024-03-01').configuration.ingress.fqdn))]

metadata.description: Network isolation applied to this deployment.
Virtual network carrying the Foundry agent subnet and the Container Apps environment. Empty unless networkIsolationMode is vnetInjection.
Subnet delegated to Foundry agent network injection.
Network Security Perimeter guarding Foundry, Key Vault and Log Analytics. Empty unless networkIsolationMode is perimeter.
Command that switches the perimeter associations from Learning to Enforced once NSPAccessLogs looks clean.

enforcePerimeterCommand.value: [if(variables('perimeterMode'), format('az network perimeter association update --name assoc-foundry --perimeter-name {0} --resource-group {1} --access-mode Enforced', variables('perimeterName'), resourceGroup().name), '(networkIsolationMode is not "perimeter")')]

metadata.description: Admin Page URL. Serves content only when Entra sign-in and an allow-list are configured.

adminPageUrl.value: [if(variables('adminUiEnabled'), format('{0}/admin', format('https://{0}', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.App/containerApps', variables('containerAppName')), '2024-03-01').configuration.ingress.fqdn)), '(disabled — supply adminEntraClientId, adminEntraClientSecret and adminAllowedPrincipals)')]

metadata.description: Archive Page URL. Administrators and explicitly allowed archive readers can browse canonical analyses.

archivePageUrl.value: [if(variables('archiveUiEnabled'), format('{0}/archive', format('https://{0}', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.App/containerApps', variables('containerAppName')), '2024-03-01').configuration.ingress.fqdn)), '(disabled — configure Entra sign-in and an archive or admin allow-list)')]

metadata.description: Microsoft Foundry project endpoint used by the Hosted Agent and persisted Prompt Agents.
Foundry Hosted Agent name that owns the complete analysis runtime.
Distinct specialist Prompt Agents orchestrated by the Hosted Agent.
Azure managed email sender domain.
Managed identity principal ID — grant it Reader on the subscriptions AzBrief should analyse.
Key Vault holding every runtime secret.
Container Apps Job that runs the daily digest.
Cron expression (UTC) the scheduler job runs on.
Blob holding the digest checkpoint. Delete it to re-analyse from the default window.
Private Blob container holding immutable canonical analysis versions.
Command that starts a digest run immediately instead of waiting for the schedule.
Command that grants the identity subscription-wide Reader access.

grantReaderCommand.value: [format('az role assignment create --assignee {0} --role Reader --scope /subscriptions/{1}', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities', variables('managedIdentityName')), '2023-01-31').principalId, subscription().subscriptionId)]

metadata.description: Command that lets the identity pull from your registry. The template wires the registry reference but cannot assign a role on a registry it does not own.

grantAcrPullCommand.value: [if(variables('hasRegistry'), format('az role assignment create --assignee {0} --role AcrPull --scope $(az acr show --name {1} --query id -o tsv)', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities', variables('managedIdentityName')), '2023-01-31').principalId, split(parameters('containerRegistryServer'), '.')[0]), '(no containerRegistryServer supplied)')]

metadata.description: Commands that roll the real AzBrief image onto BOTH the app and the scheduler job. Updating only the app leaves the nightly digest on the previous build.

deployContainerImageCommand.value: [format('az containerapp update --name {0} --resource-group {1} --image <your-registry>/azbrief-enterprise:latest ; az containerapp job update --name {2} --resource-group {3} --image <your-registry>/azbrief-enterprise:latest', variables('containerAppName'), resourceGroup().name, variables('schedulerJobName'), resourceGroup().name)]

metadata.description: Command that creates the Prompt Agent roster. ARM cannot: agents are data-plane objects, so the project stays empty until this runs.
Command that binds the six specialist Prompt Agents to the Hosted Agent deployment manifest.

configureHostedAgentCommand.value: [format('azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID={0} AZBRIEF_PROMPT_COORDINATOR_AGENT_NAME={1} AZBRIEF_PROMPT_RESOURCE_GRAPH_AGENT_NAME={2} AZBRIEF_PROMPT_AZURE_MCP_AGENT_NAME={3} AZBRIEF_PROMPT_AZURE_API_AGENT_NAME={4} AZBRIEF_PROMPT_REPORT_WRITER_AGENT_NAME={5} AZBRIEF_PROMPT_QUALITY_REVIEWER_AGENT_NAME={6}', subscription().subscriptionId, variables('foundryCoordinatorAgentName'), variables('foundryResourceGraphAgentName'), variables('foundryAzureMcpAgentName'), variables('foundryAzureApiAgentName'), variables('foundryReportWriterAgentName'), variables('foundryQualityReviewerAgentName'))]

metadata.description: Post-deployment checklist.

nextSteps.value: [format('1) Push the AzBrief control-plane image, run grantAcrPullCommand, then deployContainerImageCommand. 2) Set the azd project endpoint, run configureHostedAgentCommand, run provisionAgentsCommand and its --check, then deploy {0} from azure.yaml. 3) Grant the Hosted Agent identity Reader on every subscription it must inspect plus the service-specific data-plane roles documented in README; grantReaderCommand applies only to the Container Apps identity used by the Admin/MCP control plane. 4) Start the Container App and scheduler only after the Hosted Agent endpoint is active; they fail closed without it. 5) Optional: register an Entra app and redeploy with adminEntraClientId/Secret plus adminAllowedPrincipals and/or archiveAllowedPrincipals to enable the authenticated browser surfaces. 6) networkIsolationMode=vnetInjection: run agent provisioning/deployment from inside the virtual network, or temporarily use allowPublicAccessDuringSetup=true. 7) networkIsolationMode=perimeter: review NSPAccessLogs, then run enforcePerimeterCommand for each association.', parameters('foundryHostedAgentName'))]
